introduction: Aims to investigate how intervention and individual characteristics moderate chronic exercise effects on overall depression severity and its symptoms in older adults. To the authors' knowledge, no review attempts to uncover effects across the broadest possible range of DSM symptoms.
methodology: Planned systematic and meta-analytic review of RCTs of chronic exercise in older adults with a mean age of 60 years or above. Electronic databases will be searched from inception. Two reviewers will independently screen studies and rate quality with ROB2. A random-effects model will calculate Hedges’ g.
results: The paper is a protocol and reports no results.
discussion: The authors expect a moderate effect of exercise on depression compared to control groups. They state the conclusions may serve as a basis for evidence-based recommendations for individualized exercise programs, and the review results may reveal research gaps for further RCTs.
limitations: The authors exclude RCTs testing pharmacological treatment or psychotherapy, so no conclusions can be drawn for add-on treatment. They anticipate heterogeneous data and a wide variance in how exercise and individual characteristics are reported. Comorbidities or physical fitness level still require further research to understand their influence.

abstract_claims.q: There is high evidence that chronic exercise benefits overall depression severity in older adults.
The results of the proposed review are anticipated to have a substantial impact on research and clinical practice.
On the one hand, the review’s conclusions could form the foundation for developing evidence-based recommendations for individualized exercise programs that alleviate depression in older adults.
On the other hand, by revealing research gaps, the review results could encourage the formulation of research questions for further RCTs.

caveats.q: Abstracts from congresses and study protocols are not considered.
Intervention arms comprising a chronic exercise component additionally to other intervention components, such as nutrition, cognitive behavioral therapy, or pharmacotherapy, are not eligible.
However, this only applies if the cognitive behavioral therapy or pharmacotherapy component is specifically manipulated and tested in the study.
The intervention must last at least one week and include more than one exercise session.
Furthermore, we will only include studies in which frequency of exercise sessions, duration of exercise sessions, duration of the intervention and type of exercise are reported.
